Neither AMD nor Intel CPUs have an EFER field in the legacy SMRAM save
state area
column2: i.e. don't save/restore EFER across SMM transitions.  KVM

column1: somewhat models this
column2: e.g. doesn't clear EFER on entry to SMM if the

column1: guest doesn't support long mode.  But during RSM
clears EFER so that it can get back to pure 32-bit mode in order to
start loading CRs with their actual non-SMM values.
Clear EFER only when it will be written when loading the non-SMM state
so as to preserve bits that can theoretically be set on 32-bit vCPUs
e.g. KVM always emulates EFER_SCE.
And because CR4.PAE is cleared only to play nice with EFER
code in the long mode check as well.  Note
compiler warning about cr4 being consumed uninitialized.  Re-read CR4
even though it's technically unnecessary
column2: as doing so allows for more

column1: readable code and RSM emulation is not a performance critical path.
